title: Triage the three red last-access tests (LastAccessTests.AFolderThatRefusesWriteAttributes..., HeldOpenTreeTests.TheScanChangesNoEntrysMetadata, HeldOpenTreeTests.APlainListingOfTheControlFolderMovesItsLastAccessTime): environment fault or real scan side effect
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: observed: the scan reports it kept 7 of the 7 folders' last-access times it asked to keep, but only 4 of the 7 folders under C:\WINDOWS\Temp\fsa-sl096-f71d95e52bfd4f25961f2430b9dbe375 still read 48 h old: 3 had their last access moved to now (<root>, plain, links).
Each of the three red tests is diagnosed as an environment fault or a real scan side effect, with measured evidence (derived from the title and 'never diagnosed'): partial

The full suite is green as the project runs it: pwsh eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx in the engine's environment, where TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP (derived from 'Until they are triaged the full suite is never green'): missing

A real scan side effect in the last-access area (SC-070/074: the scan changes no entry's metadata, and its kept counters are true) is detectable, not hidden in the noise (derived from 'a regression in that area would hide in the noise'): missing
kept-counter-uncounts-parent-of-child-keep-open-under-system: Attempted-open rule under-counts: tree (d) kept 0, R still 48 h old (truth 1); a=1, b=4 correct
deepest-first-backdating-under-windows-temp: Back-dating deepest-first still fails 2 of 23 under C:\WINDOWS\TEMP in 3 of 3 runs; user TEMP 23/23

Where the TEMP problem is fixed: - TempTree redirect (chosen; works whatever launches the suite); - the engine launching with the HKCU TEMP (spike 5 go; outside this repo); - TempTree refusing a %SystemRoot% TEMP outright (keeps the suite red under the engine).

Whether 'Counting-rule tests build real NTFS trees in %TEMP%' is honoured by %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp when the process TEMP is the machine's. This design reads it as the user's own TEMP (the HKCU value, measured). A stricter reader may disagree.
kept == unmoved (chosen; also catches under-counting, and trips if luafv stops acting) vs kept <= unmoved (the bug test's weaker form, which would not trip on a machine without luafv).
Whether default-suite Facts should write into C:\Windows\Temp at all, a folder this user cannot list, so a failed cleanup there is unrecoverable without an administrator.
Whether the counter correction deserves a KnownWorkarounds checkbox. This design says no: it changes no scan behaviour and corrects this project's own false count.
Parent identity in the correction: path text in a per-scan set (chosen) vs a per-folder flag or index carried by the walk (no path handling, but it changes the walk's work items).
The engine launching test runs with the HKCU TEMP/TMP (spike 5): taad_v3's launch.py is outside this repository.
Routing SyncRootRig/CloudRig (opt-in Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT) through TempTree's root choice: filed by the design. CloudPlaceholderTests.cs is exempt from rule 2 by name until then.
Any change that avoids the parent's last-access move (plain-open children, holding parent handles): Q-207 decided against it, and Q-159 defers it.
Widening the correction to %ProgramData%/%ProgramFiles%: unmeasured, and writing there is the person's step.
A KnownWorkarounds entry or an in-app notice: no app behaviour steps around luafv. The scan does what it did, the correction fixes this project's own count, and the redirect lives in test fixtures.
Keying the per-scan set by store entry index (m6, waived and carried as SC-173): the design's path-text set is built.
A GetFinalPathNameByHandleW comparison for roots reaching the Windows folder by another spelling (m9, waived and carried as SC-176): recorded as a limit only.

Removing the survey's leftover C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-sl096survey-<8 hex> folder: its name cannot be listed by this user, and the admin operations on offer (whoami, read-denied-folders, which returns counts and never names) cannot find it.

Engine mutation runner: restoring a mutated file with Copy-Item kept its older timestamp, and MSBuild then skipped the rebuild. The DLL kept the mutated code and the next test run failed spuriously (seen in this build: the bug test went red until Scanner.cs was touched). When the engine puts a mutated file back, it should touch it or force a rebuild.
taad_v3 launch.py: give test runs the user's HKCU TEMP/TMP (spike 5 measured 23/23 with it).
Slice: route SyncRootRig/CloudRig through TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot and drop CloudPlaceholderTests.cs from rule 2's except_files.
Person (admin): confirm luafv.sys is the driver (fltmc, or a trace), and remove the survey's leftover folder in C:\Windows\Temp.
Person: measure whether a write-class child open moves the parent in %ProgramData% and %ProgramFiles%. If it does, widen WindowsFolderFromEnvironment's location list.
Person: run LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests and the 23 last-access tests on Windows 10 (Q-205).
Person: decide whether docs/design/SL-096-last-access-under-windows-temp.md closes Q-190.
SC-174 (m7) can likely close: TempTree.Outside() now builds under the root the tree was given.

.taad-scratch/ (investigation probes, run logs, and small trees under .taad-scratch/temp/fsa-tests) is untracked in this worktree and was left untouched. Someone should decide whether it is committed or discarded.

deviation: Rule 1's Trait clause is `\bTrait(Attribute)?\s*\(`, not the critique's `\[\s*Trait\s*\(`. The critique's form misses `[Fact, Trait("Network", ...)]`, which the design's own pattern caught (corpus S18/S19), and `[TraitAttribute(...)]` (S27). The custom-attribute pattern starts at `[` or `,` rather than `[` alone, to catch `[Fact, WindowsTempFact]` (S23). `Skip\s*=` became `\bSkip\w*\s*=`, to catch xUnit v3's SkipWhen/SkipUnless on data rows (S05).

deviation: The optional `:\s*(FactAttribute|TheoryAttribute)\b` went into SL-096's settled rule 1, not into the twinned CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped. Changing a twinned rule would move the parity counts that RuleCases and SettledCountProbe pin literally (Q-085).

deviation: Rule 2 bans more than M1's single `Path\.GetTempPath\s*\(`, because the obligation says close the class. It also bans GetTempFileName, Directory.CreateTempSubdirectory, GetEnvironmentVariable/ExpandEnvironmentVariables of TEMP/TMP/SystemRoot/windir, other drive letters, forward slashes, a lower-case "temp" and `+` concatenation. Each is a corpus row.

deviation: Added LastAccessRuleCorpusTests.TheWindowsFolderFactsRunInTheDefaultSuite, a reflection check that the design did not name. It closes the members of m2's class that no line pattern can see: a non-public class, a deleted [Fact], a foreign attribute, a by-name clause in the default filter.

deviation: TempTree's root is no longer a static field. It is chosen on each construction and kept in an instance field, so a refusal is a named InvalidOperationException rather than a TypeInitializationException that poisons every test. As a consequence Outside() now builds beside the tree's own root. That is what waived O-023 (m7, carried as SC-174) asked for; it fell out of the structure rather than being built on purpose.

deviation: The engine-appended SL-096 yaml entries were reformatted: each name on one line and patterns single-quoted, with the same YAML values. This lets the existing SettledPatterns reader, made internal, feed them to the corpus tests. The `because` texts were updated for M1/m2.
deviation: LastAccessRuleCorpusTests builds the route rule's name from two string pieces, so the file does not spell `%SystemRoot%\Temp` and need its own exemption from the rule it tests.

deviation: The cases for the whole suite under each TEMP (C-006, C-007) use `dotnet test -e TEMP=... -e TMP=...` rather than the design's `$env:TEMP=...;` form, which is shell syntax the engine's commands cannot carry. -e was shown to reach the test host: a bogus TEMP crashed it. C-007's path is this machine's own %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, written out.

O-015 not done: Not measurable here: no Windows 10 machine exists (Q-205), and writing test folders under %ProgramData% or %ProgramFiles% is the person's step. The triage doc and the ScanResult contract record both as unmeasured and uncorrected.

drift: TempTree.ChooseTestsRoot (TempTree.cs:54-68) has two branches the design did not name and the build did not declare. An empty or unqualified Windows folder uses TEMP as-is. An empty or unqualified LOCALAPPDATA is refused by name. Both are tested (TempTreeRootTests WithNoWindowsFolderNamedTheTempIsUsedAsItIs and the "" refusal row). They are harmless and consistent with review m1.

drift: The Scanner's class remarks (Scanner.cs:22-26) say a child's kept open moves its parent's last access 'under the Windows folder' in general. Only %SystemRoot%\Temp was measured. ScanResult.LastAccessKept's remarks state that limit precisely, so the class summary is the looser of the two texts.
not reviewed: .taad/slices/SL-096/critique-1.json, critique-review-1.json, design-slice-1.json, index.json: engine records, not code. I read none of them; the brief carried what I needed.
not reviewed: tests/bugs/SL-096-LastAccessUnderWindowsTemp/*: the engine's unchanged acceptance test. I only spot-read its assertions (line 139, `LastAccessKept <= unmoved`) and ran it.

not reached: Windows 10: neither LastAccessUnderSystemRootTests nor the 23 last-access tests were run there (no machine; Q-205). If luafv does not move parents there, the kept == still-old tests would go red, because the correction would count out parents that never moved.

not reached: %ProgramData% and %ProgramFiles%: whether a child's write-class open moves its parent there is unmeasured. Measuring it means writing outside this tree, or an administrator. The correction covers %SystemRoot% only.

not reached: Whether luafv.sys itself issues the parent query: it needs fltmc or a trace as an administrator. Neither offered operation (whoami, read-denied-folders) can do it, so I did not ask for one.

not reached: Whether the bug test's two runs during my mutations left C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-sl096-<guid> trees behind. C:\Windows\Temp cannot be listed by this user. The test deletes with Directory.Delete, which the survey showed works there, but nothing confirms it. The survey's earlier leftover (fsa-sl096survey-<8 hex>) and the code review's probable C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\fsa-parity-case-<10 hex> also still need an administrator to remove them.

not reached: The opt-in Cloud=CF-SYNC-ROOT, Network=SMB-LOOPBACK and Network=TEST-NET-1 tests were not run. The default filter excludes them, and SyncRootRig is not yet routed through TempTree; that is filed.

not reached: The app shows no last-access counters (Q-103/Q-159). The real publish run therefore shows only that the shipped exe still scans a Windows-folder root to completion, not the corrected count in the app.
not reached: The design's TempTree root-choice branches for a SYSTEM or service profile were exercised only as a pure function, not by running the suite as LocalSystem or a service account.

critique missed: The critique filed M1 on architecture rule 2 and proposed adding `Path\.GetTempPath\s*\(`. It checked only that the rule's patterns matched nothing in Core.Tests today. It never fed the patterns this repo's own path spellings. Pattern 2 needs a `"` straight before the drive letter and pattern 1 needs `)` straight after SpecialFolder.Windows. That lets through `@"\\?\C:\Windows\Temp\..."` (the extended form used in LongPath.ToExtended and TempTree.ExtendedRoot), `Path.Combine(@"C:\", "Windows", "Temp")`, %SystemDrive%\Windows\Temp, and the GetFolderPath(SpecialFolder.Windows, SpecialFolderOption.X) overload. A check would be to run the proposed rule over a corpus of each spelling the codebase already uses before calling the class closed.

critique missed: The critique's own proposed fix for m2 was incomplete. `\[\s*Trait\s*\(` misses `[Fact, Trait("Network", ...)]` and `[TraitAttribute(...)]`. `Skip\s*=` misses SkipWhen and SkipUnless on data rows. The custom-attribute pattern must also start at `,`, not only `[`, to catch `[Fact, WindowsTempFact]`. The critique did not try its regexes against the bug test's own [WindowsTempFact] or any xUnit v3 skip form.

critique missed: The design carried 'luafv moves the parent the same way on Windows 10, and in %ProgramData% and %ProgramFiles%' as a must-verify precondition and also filed it for a person. The critique did not ask which stage could discharge it. The answer was none: no Windows 10 machine exists, writing to ProgramData is outside what stages may touch, and Program Files needs an administrator. The obligation was aimed at validate and cost a halted validate #1 and a second lap.

critique missed: The design records 'Only C:\Windows\Temp was measured' and still decides the correction's scope is all of %SystemRoot%, and writes Scanner's class remarks as 'under the Windows folder' in general. The critique did not ask what happens in a writable subfolder of C:\Windows other than Temp where luafv may not move the parent. The correction would under-count there, and the == Facts cover only Temp.

still unknown: Does a successful child keep-open move its parent in writable folders under C:\Windows other than Temp (for example Tasks, Tracing, Registration\CRMLog)? Russinovich's quote says luafv excludes 'some specific subdirectories'. The correction fires for all of %SystemRoot% on a structural rule, so if the parent does not move there, kept under-counts. Settle this before Q-159 is reopened for file-age features, because that is when LastAccessKept stops being internal.

still unknown: Can an administrator confirm with fltmc or a trace that luafv.sys is the component that stamps the parent? So far this rests on correlation with the 'Luaf' pool tag (2 allocations per write-class open, none otherwise). The code is keyed on location, not driver, but the triage doc, the ScanResult remarks and the Scanner remarks all name luafv.

still unknown: Do the five default-suite Windows-folder Facts stay green on a machine where the user cannot create folders under C:\Windows\Temp\fsa-tests, or where luafv does not move parents (Windows 10, Q-205)? The Facts assert kept == still-old and never skip, so they would go red on both. Nobody has said whether a red there is the intended signal or an environmental false alarm.

went wrong: Rule 2 was recorded as closed as a class (O-016, a 34-row corpus), but the code review's second adversarial round found six spellings of the Windows Temp folder quiet against it. The finding was waived to SC-177 as 'does not weigh a lap on its own'. The default-suite guard rail therefore ships claiming more than it covers.

went wrong: Two of the critique's proposed fix patterns (M1, m2) were wrong or incomplete and reached the builder as the fix. The builder had to deviate on rule 1 and the code review found the rule 2 gap. No gate ran the proposed regexes against a corpus first, and critique-review was sized away for this medium, single-designer slice.
went wrong: validate-slice ran twice. O-015 was aimed at validate although the design had already filed it for a person, and the second pass learned nothing new.

went wrong: The stale-DLL trap after restoring a mutated file hit twice. Spike 3 threw away three runs (c1-c3). In the build, the bug test and the first full-suite attempt went red spuriously. The design had already recorded the trap as a measured claim, with 'Nothing breaks'.

went wrong: Loop stages left unrecoverable folders in C:\Windows\Temp: the survey's fsa-sl096survey-<8 hex>, the code review's probable fsa-parity-case-<10 hex>, and validate's two bug-test mutation runs (cleanup unverifiable). All need an administrator.

went wrong: Five minor findings were waived or carried (SC-173 to SC-177). m7 (SC-174) was then fixed incidentally by the build, so the backlog holds a stale item. The deferred RuleCases finding points at a follow-up slice whose text does not mention RuleCases.
went wrong: The bug report was only a title. The three build-check criteria were derived from that title, and the only contract was the engine's reproduction test.
